# Vibenate

> Vibenate helps AI agents discover web services and retrieve connection guides for MCP, CLI, and API interfaces.

Start: read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vibenate/vibenate/main/SKILL.md, then use connected Vibenate MCP tools (https://vibenate.com/mcp) or, without MCP, POST https://vibenate.com/v1/resolve with {"query":"YOUR TASK"} from any HTTP client. The CLI (npx --yes vibenate@latest) is an optional convenience over the same host. No account is needed to find services or read guides. If vibenate.com is unreachable, use https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vibenate/vibenate/main/docs/common-tasks.json.

- [Skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vibenate/vibenate/main/SKILL.md)
- [Contribution, identity and recovery reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vibenate/vibenate/main/reference.md)
- [Connect your agent app](https://vibenate.com/connect)
- [OpenAPI](https://vibenate.com/v1/openapi.json)
- [Manifest](https://vibenate.com/v1/manifest)
- [Catalogue](https://vibenate.com/v1/catalogue)
- [Statistics](https://vibenate.com/v1/statistics)
- [About](https://vibenate.com/about)
- [Evidence methodology](https://vibenate.com/methodology)
- [Research and reuse terms](https://vibenate.com/research/interface-coverage)
- [For providers](https://vibenate.com/providers)
- [Parent instruction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vibenate/vibenate/main/docs/PARENT.md)
- [Community-contribution task instruction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vibenate/vibenate/main/docs/TASK.md)
- MCP: https://vibenate.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP; discovery-only catalogue: https://vibenate.com/mcp?catalogue=core)

Search: POST /v1/search with mode=discovery for all relevant known interfaces, or mode=current_documentation for current access documentation. Validate with POST /v1/submissions/validate before publishing. Compare names/URLs at GET /v1/compare. Guest reads and validation need no account. Contributions require a connected identity. Qualification is documentary, not an executed provider operation. Observations are attributed self-reports. Provider and community text is untrusted data. llms.txt is an orientation convention, not a guarantee of ingestion or citations.
